title: Eventual vanishing of a stage section in the supplied cocone
statement: For the data of the finite-site section comparison theorem, if a stage element x has zero image under K.ι, then some refinement map D.map b sends x to zero.

source.place: Tag 0A35, stage section presentation and equality paragraphs; abelian extension via sites-modules.tex Tag 03CO

proof.text: A presentation of Y is (t,W,p), with t in Under(i), W in F(t.right), and p:V(t.right)(W)=Y. A refinement b:t to t-prime carries W to W-prime, with endpoint transports. Nonemptiness follows by lifting Y using hobjects and moving its stage to a common stage with i. Under(i) is filtered. A common stage for two presentations followed by eventual equality of their object representatives supplies a common refinement. Filteredness equalizes parallel refinements. Evaluating the unique unit-characterized adjunct transition at W gives the group transition; uniqueness proves identity and composition. Lift restriction arrows using harrows, move to a common stage with i and the chosen presentations, and correct endpoints using hobjects. Eventual arrow equality proves independence of the lift; lifting finite collections proves the presheaf laws. Refinements of any fixed presentation are final: lift its representative and any other representative to a common stage and use eventual object equality, then equalize parallel refinements. Equivalently apply the dual cofiltered initiality criterion.

Take the filtered colimit of the inverse-image section groups over these presentations. Lift a restriction arrow to a common stage. The unit equations determine transition sheaf maps uniquely by the stage adjunction, so eventual equality and naturality make restriction independent of its lift and prove the identity and composition laws. All restrictions are additive. Every Q cover is an image finite stage cover by hQ and hfinite. Covering pullbacks are preserved. Lift the finitely many matching-family objects and equations to one stage; filtered group colimits commute with the finite products and equalizers for the stage sheaf condition. This makes the constructed abelian presheaf a sheaf. An empty cover gives its zero section group.

Maps from this sheaf to an arbitrary abelian sheaf T are compatible maps on stage section groups. Moving a presentation to its identity refinement identifies each compatible family with a stage sheaf map L_t to V_t restriction of T. The stage adjunction transposes this to a map G to V_i restriction of T; compatibility with the source unit forces the adjunct to be the same for all t. Conversely such a map supplies each stage adjunct, and the colimit property assembles the section maps. The inverse homEquiv equations and colimit hom_ext show that these correspondences are mutually inverse and natural in T. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the constructed sheaf with the canonical V_i inverse image, compatibly with its unit.

At V_i(U), carried-U presentations are final by the common-stage and eventual-object/arrow equality argument. Identify the constructed sheaf with the canonical inverse image by the preceding adjunction argument. Use hK to transfer the zero-image hypothesis to that filtered presentation colimit. Equality with the zero representative occurs at a common refinement; equalize the two outgoing refinement arrows and pass to a carried-U refinement. Unit uniqueness identifies the maps with the supplied theta. Use hD and injectivity of E at the refined stage to conclude D.map b x = 0. No source-unit zero-detection or theorem depending on the parent comparison is used.

theorem colimit_site_finite_section_eventual_zero
    (J : Type u) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] (F : J ⥤ Cat.{u, u})
    (P : ∀ j : J, Precoverage (F.obj j))
    [∀ j, (P j).HasIsos] [∀ j, (P j).IsStableUnderFiniteComposition]
    [∀ j, (P j).IsStableUnderFiniteBaseChange] [∀ j, (P j).HasPullbacks]
    (hfinite : ∀ (j : J) (X : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X), R ∈ P j X →
      Finite R.uncurry)
    (hcover : ∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k) (X : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X),
      R ∈ P j X → R.map (F.map a).toFunctor ∈ P k ((F.map a).toFunctor.obj X))
    (hpullback : ∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k) (X Y Z : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X),
      R ∈ P j X → ∀ (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ X), R f →
        PreservesLimit (cospan f g) (F.map a).toFunctor)
    [∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k),
      (F.map a).toFunctor.IsContinuous (P j).toGrothendieck (P k).toGrothendieck]
    (V : Cocone F)
    (hobjects : IsColimit (Cat.objects.mapCocone V))
    (harrows : IsColimit (Cat.arrows.mapCocone V))
    (Q : Precoverage V.pt)
    [Q.HasIsos] [Q.IsStableUnderFiniteComposition]
    [Q.IsStableUnderFiniteBaseChange] [Q.HasPullbacks]
    (hQ : (∀ (Y : V.pt) (R : Presieve Y), R ∈ Q Y ↔
          ∃ (j : J) (X : F.obj j) (S : Presieve X) (h : (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.obj X = Y),
            S ∈ P j X ∧ h ▸ S.map (V.ι.app j).toFunctor = R))
    (hVpullback : (∀ (j : J) (X Y Z : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X), R ∈ P j X →
            ∀ (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ X), R f →
              PreservesLimit (cospan f g) (V.ι.app j).toFunctor))
    [∀ j : J, (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.IsContinuous
      (P j).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck]
    (i : J) (G : Sheaf (P i).toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (α : ∀ t : Under i,
      (sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P i).toGrothendieck (P
        t.right).toGrothendieck).obj G ⟶
      ((V.ι.app t.right).toFunctor.sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
        t.right).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).obj
        ((sheafPullback (V.ι.app i).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P i).toGrothendieck
          Q.toGrothendieck).obj G))
    (θ : ∀ (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t'),
      (sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P i).toGrothendieck (P
        t.right).toGrothendieck).obj G ⟶
      ((F.map b.right).toFunctor.sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
        t.right).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck).obj
        ((sheafPullback (F.map t'.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P i).toGrothendieck (P
          t'.right).toGrothendieck).obj G))
    (hα : ∀ (t : Under i) (X : F.obj i),
      Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
        i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app (op X) ≫ (α t).hom.app
        (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj X))) =
      Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (V.ι.app i).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
        i).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app (op X)))
    (hθ : ∀ (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t') (X : F.obj i),
      Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
        i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app (op X) ≫
        (θ t t' b).hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj X))) =
      Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t'.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
        i).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app (op X)))
    (U : F.obj i)
    (D : Under i ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (E : ∀ t : Under i, D.obj t ≅
      ((sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P i).toGrothendieck (P
        t.right).toGrothendieck).obj G).obj.obj (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U)))
    (K : Cocone D) (e : K.pt ≅ ((sheafPullback (V.ι.app i).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
      i).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).obj G).obj.obj (op ((V.ι.app i).toFunctor.obj U)))
    (hK : ∀ t : Under i, Arrow.mk (K.ι.app t ≫ e.hom) =
      Arrow.mk ((E t).hom ≫ (α t).hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U))))
    (hD : ∀ (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t'),
      Arrow.mk ((E t).hom ≫ (θ t t' b).hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U))) =
      Arrow.mk (D.map b ≫ (E t').hom)) :
    ∀ (t : Under i) (x : D.obj t), (K.ι.app t).hom x = 0 →
      ∃ (t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t'), (D.map b).hom x = 0
